editions.text:
Yesterday brought 282 feeder visits, slightly exceeding the recent weekly average of 278.7. The number of detected species dropped to 16, down from the previous seven-day average of 20.1, due to the absence of regulars such as the Mourning Dove and Ruby-throated Hummingbird, which had been recorded on every day of the prior week.

A second microphone began listening at 10:44, operating alongside the original unit. The Rose-breasted Grosbeak returned to the list after a seven-day absence, adding to the 16 species detected, while the Tufted Titmouse and Carolina Chickadee remained consistent presences.

Visual observations highlighted the Tufted Titmouse, which recorded the highest number of visits with 139, followed by the Carolina Chickadee with 63. A refill on the seed and nectar feeders the previous evening maintained the flow of regulars like the Northern Cardinal and House Finch. The day ended with a final visual of a Northern Cardinal.
